newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Daschle says Republican tax cut too high.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Daschle says Republican tax cut too high.

text.p: Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said Republicans have been boosting the size of their tax cut proposal, making more difficult any compromise on spending cuts to reach a balanced budget.

Speaking to reporters, the South Dakota Democrat said his party is prepared to show some flexibility on domestic spending cuts, but Republican efforts to add to the size of tax cuts impeded negotiations. "Republicans are moving in the opposite direction on tax cuts. Instead of moving closer, they are moving farther away," he said.

House Speaker Newt Gingrich's call to eliminate capital gains taxes and estate taxes would cost $300 billion over five years, a sizeable increase from the previous Republican tax cut plans which were expected to cost $185 billion over five years.
House and Senate leaders of both parties are to meet President Clinton next week to discuss the budget talks and other issues including foreign policy, Daschle said.
Daschle said it was too soon for Clinton to become personally involved in the budget negotiations, and added that Democrats would prefer the sessions be held in public.
